text: Agile methodology is a popular way of managing projects, especially in software development. Instead of planning everything at the start, teams work in short cycles called sprints, usually lasting two to four weeks. Before each sprint, the team chooses items from the backlog, a prioritised list of tasks often written as user stories that describe what users need. Every day, team members hold short meetings called standups to share progress and problems. This iterative development approach allows teams to deliver working products quickly, get feedback, and improve continuously. Agile helps teams stay flexible and respond to change.
